summary: Configured /etc/logrotate.d/inventory on node1 to rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily, keep 7 compressed rotations, and use copytruncate so the writing application is never interrupted. Verified rotation behavior live with a simulated continuously-appending writer, confirmed config and data survive a full node restart, and confirmed boot identity changed to prove a genuine reboot occurred.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: RHEL 10, logrotate 3.22.0 installed, /var/log/inventory/app.log present, no active writer process or systemd service found for the app, logrotate.timer active/enabled
Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory with daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate
Launched a background shell loop appending heartbeat lines to app.log to simulate the application writer
Forced rotation with logrotate -f -v, confirmed app.log.1.gz created and app.log truncated in place via copytruncate
Confirmed the simulated writer process kept running and continued appending new lines to app.log immediately after rotation, with prior content preserved in app.log.1.gz
Stopped and cleaned up the simulated writer process
Captured baseline boot_id, logrotate.timer status, and config/log data health on node1
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect); single node only, no power-off used
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again, confirmed boot_id changed from 4ebdfa06-919e-48a9-8a15-475d9007662c to fce34599-49f6-489a-89e1-2a8e857f177a
Verified post-restart recovery: logrotate.timer active/enabled and scheduled, /etc/logrotate.d/inventory persisted, app.log and app.log.1.gz data intact, dry-run rotation logic still correctly parsed

evidence.requirement: logrotate config created: daily rotation, keep 7 compressed rotations
evidence.summary: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory with daily, rotate 7, compress, copytruncate and validated syntax via logrotate -d debug run.

Started a continuously-appending simulated app writer, forced rotation (app.log.1.gz created, app.log truncated via copytruncate), then showed the writer process was still running and new heartbeat lines kept appending to app.log immediately after rotation while pre-rotation content was preserved in app.log.1.gz.
Forced rotation produced a gzip-compressed app.log.1.gz; zcat confirmed original pre-rotation log lines were preserved intact.
Captured boot_id 4ebdfa06-919e-48a9-8a15-475d9007662c, confirmed logrotate.timer active, config file present, and dry-run rotation logic correct prior to restart.
Issued backgrounded systemctl reboot so the exec call returned before disconnect; subsequent exec calls failed with connection reset/timeout, confirming the node went down.

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: After polling until exec succeeded again, boot_id read fce34599-49f6-489a-89e1-2a8e857f177a, differing from the pre-restart value, proving an actual reboot occurred.

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required services and data
evidence.summary: Post-restart check showed logrotate.timer active/enabled and scheduled, /etc/logrotate.d/inventory config persisted, app.log and app.log.1.gz data intact, and logrotate dry-run still correctly recognizing the daily/7-rotation policy.
